Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Chad Bowes and Tim Seifert are the two openers for New Zealand. Sri Lanka going with spin straightaway as Maheesh Theekshana has the new ball in hand. Here we go..
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Sri Lanka have posted a well below-par total on the board and will need something special from their bowlers to defend it. New Zealand will be confident of gunning this down and keep their record of being unbeaten in international matches at this ground intact. Let's see how the chase unfolds.

The man of the moment, Adam Milne is up for a quick chat. He says that it is a nice feeling to get a fi-fer. Also it was necessary to come stronger after the Super Over loss. Mentions the spinners did really well to get things under control in the middle over. Informs that he just tried to go full and straight, in the final over. Ends by saying that it is a nice feeling leading the time out of the park, with the ball in hand.

New Zealand showed great fight and determination and Tom Latham used all of his bowling resources really well. There were a few expensive overs here and there, but they were able to pull things back with wickets at regular intervals and did not allow Sri Lanka to get the momentum. Adam Milne was the pick of the bowlers with his five-wicket haul. Benjamin Lister got a couple of wickets while everyone else got one to their name excet for James Neesham.

Sri Lanka will be very disappointed as they know that they could have got a lot more considering the start they got. Even though they lost both openers inside the Powerplay, the scoring rate was good. The partnership between Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Perera of 62 runs gave them the platform to go big, but both got dismissed in their thirties and in quick succession which put a brake on their innings. However, Charith Asalanka continued his good form and played a good cameo without much support on the other end. From 82/2 in ten overs to 141 all out, this has been an extraordinary collapse for them and they are staring down the barrel now.

A dominating display from the Kiwis! After the narrow Super-Over defeat in the first T20I, the hosts have comeback really well and restricted the Lankans to just 140 runs thanks to a brilliant five-wicket haul from Adam Milne. They will be the happier side going into the break and it looks like we will be heading for a decider in this series.

Commentary.Commentary: Full, on the pads. Dhananjaya de Silva flicks it to deep square leg and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Adam Milne to Dhananjaya de Silva, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dhananjaya de Silva comes in to bat now.

OUT! TAKEN! Adam Milne gets his man this time, and no review needed! He serves this full and outside off, Pathum Nissanka once again goes for the big slog, but only manages to slice it in the air as the ball goes in the air towards third man where Benjamin Lister runs forward and takes a good low catch. Sri Lanka have lost both openers now!
Commentary.Howout: c Benjamin Lister b Adam Milne
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Benjamin Lister b Adam Milne.

Commentary.Commentary: A huge shout for LBW, but the umpire says no! Tom Latham goes for the review after some discussion. Adam Milne bowls this on a good length and on off, shaping in, Pathum Nissanka swings across the line, but misses and gets hit high on the pads. The UltraEdge shows no bat involved, but Ball Tracking confirms that it is going over the wickets. Nissanka survives anf the Kiwis lose the review!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Adam Milne bangs this onto the pitch and on middle, shaping away, Kusal Perera looks to heave it away, but misses and Tom Latham behind the stumps gets surprised and only manages to parry it towards fine leg. A bye is taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Adam Milne to Kusal Perera, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Kusal Mendis pats it down towards point where there is a slight misfield, but no harm done.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Adam Milne to Kusal Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change. Adam Milne (1-0-8-0) is back into the attack.
Fuller again and on off, Kusal Perera drives it wide of mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Henry Shipley to Kusal Perera, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller and on off, Kusal Perera drills it wide of mid off as Adam Milne chase it down well and keeps it inside. Two runs taken!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Henry Shipley to Kusal Perera, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Another batter gets off the mark with a big hit! Henry Shipley lands this short and around off, Kusal Perera this time gets on top of it and swots it over the long on fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Henry Shipley to Kusal Perera, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a hard length and outside off, angling away once more, Kusal Perera looks to guide it away, but gets beaten again.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Henry Shipley to Kusal Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEAUTY! This is short of a length and around leg, angling away with some extra bounce, Kusal Perera looks to work it away, but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Henry Shipley to Kusal Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Henry Shipley starts with a back-of-a-length delivery, on middle, Pathum Nissanka pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Henry Shipley to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Kusal Perera dabs it down towards point. End of a successful over for the Kiwis!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Benjamin Lister to Kusal Perera, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kusal Perera is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Benjamin Lister draws first blood! A good comeback from him as Kusal Mendis goes back to the hut. This is full again and around off this time, angling away, Kusal Mendis looks to flick it, but closes the face of the bat early and gets a top edge as the ball flies high in the air and Tom Latham behind the stumps calls for it, moves to his right and pouches it safely in his gloves. Sri Lanka lose their first wicket!
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Latham b Benjamin Lister
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Benjamin Lister to Kusal Mendis, OUT! c Tom Latham b Benjamin Lister.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A boundary now! Benjamin Lister pitches this one up, on leg, Kusal Mendis gets under it and whips it wide of mid on for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Benjamin Lister to Kusal Mendis, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Kusal Mendis gets off the mark in style now! Benjamin Lister lands this short and around leg, Kusal Mendis stays there and hooks it over the fine leg fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Benjamin Lister to Kusal Mendis, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a good length and on off, Kusal Mendis taps it in front of short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Benjamin Lister to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Benjamin Lister begins with a full delivery, on off, Kusal Mendis pushes it towards short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Benjamin Lister to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Benjamin Lister to share the new ball.
FOUR! A boundary straightaway from the new bat! This is short and on middle, Pathum Nissanka once again pulls it nice and hard towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WHAT! The ball is leaving Adam Milne's arm like a bullet. Time to exchange the bat now, as the handle comes off this one for Pathum Nissanka.
We have a broken bat! Adam Milne serves this on a hard length and on off, Pathum Nissanka defends it from the splice of the bat and the handle is broken. He will need a new one now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pathum Nissanka and Sri Lanka are finally underway and in style! Adam Milne lands this short and on middle, sits up nicely, Pathum Nissanka picks up the length early, swivels and pulls it towards the deep square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Three dots in a row! This is full again and on middle, nips away, Pathum Nissanka pushes it towards short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes a bit fuller now, on middle, swinging away in the air, Pathum Nissanka knocks it with the outer half of his bat towards covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Adam Milne starts with a hard-length delivery, on middle, shaping away a shy bit, Pathum Nissanka keeps it out on the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Adam Milne to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The match is set to begin. The New Zealand players make their way out on the field. Followed by Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis. It will be Adam Milne to start with the new ball. Here we go...

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Kusal Mendis, Pathum Nissanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, Kusal Perera (WK), Charith Asalanka, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dasun Shanaka (C), Kasun Rajitha (In for Chamika Karunaratne), Maheesh Theekshana, Dilshan Madushanka, Pramod Madushan.
New Zealand (Unchanged playing XI) - Chad Bowes, Tim Seifert, Tom Latham (C/ WK), Daryl Mitchell, Mark Chapman, James Neesham, Rachin Ravindra, Adam Milne, Henry Shipley, Ish Sodhi, Benjamin Lister.
TOSS - New Zealand win the toss and have opted to BOWL first.

Update - After this series gets over, Dasun Shanaka will be heading down to India to play for Gujarat in the Indian T20 League. He has been selected as a replacement of Kane Williamson, who suffered a knee injury during the first match of the season, and was forced to make his way out of the tournament. The ex-Kiwi skipper has come back to New Zealand and would be going through his recovery. Hopefully, we are able to see him back on the field, sooner rather than later.

New Zealand, on the other hand will be disappointed with the loss, but their never say die attitude was on show. Daryl Mitchell was brilliant once again and when all looked lost needing seven of the final delivery, Ish Sodhi smashed a six to tie the game. However, they couldn't turn up in the Super Over falling to a defeat. They have lost quite a few players to the Indian T20 League, but still have managed to put on a decent fight. Their bowling is a bit inexperienced, but this is their chance to show their talent against a strong opposition. Will they fight back and level the series? Or will the Lankans take an unassailable lead? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Sri Lanka put on their best performance in the last game and finally got their first win of this tour. Their batters stepped up big time to put on a good score while the bowling could have been better and they will need to improve that. However, Maheesh Theekshana held his nerve well and bowled a brilliant Super Over, conceding just eight runs which set the platform perfectly for Charith Asalanka to get them over the line after scoring a brilliant fifty in the game. They will want to do more of the same and get another win over the Kiwis.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 2nd T20I of this three-match series between New Zealand and Sri Lanka at the University Oval in Dunedin in New Zealand. The first game was a nail-biter as the Lankans edged past the Kiwis in a Super Over and took a 1-0 lead and will look to seal the series in this game only while the hosts will want to get the better of the visitors and take the series to a decider.
... Match Day ...

After clinching a victory in an action-packed thriller that went down to a super over in the first T20I, the visitors Sri Lanka would be looking to seal the series with a victory in the second T20I against the Kiwis. Sri Lanka batted amazingly in the first game and posted 196 on the board. The batters clicked collectively for the first time on this tour and they managed to carve their way towards the first victory of this tour courtesy of a boundary from the bat of Charith Asalanka in the super over. The bowling was decent too in the first T20I. Kusal Mendis is the key for the visitors as he can take the game away from any opponent on his day while the bowling department will be heavily reliant on the broad shoulders of Maheesh Theekshana and Wanindu Hasaranga yet again. New Zealand too had a decent outing and the never give up attitude of the Kiwis was key for them to take the game as deep as they did in the first T20I. The top order failed to give them a good start but Daryl Mitchell cleaned the scrap for them and helped them to a super over which they lost eventually. The hosts would be looking to get level in the series with a victory in the second T20I and a lot would depend on Daryl Mitchell as he holds the key for the Kiwis being their premium 3-D players. Expect a thriller as these two consistently improving sides face each other yet again.
